parole.significato: tree or fruit of Phyllanthus emblica, emblic myrobalan or emblic
parole.testo: Via Middle Persian (from which Classical Persian آمله (âmula)) from Sanskrit आमलक (āmalaka), आमलकी (āmalakī) of this meaning.

parole.significato: triphala, compound drug of the three myrobalans
parole.testo: From Middle Persian – Persian اطریفل (etrifal) –, from Sanskrit त्रिफला (triphalā).

parole.significato: black myrobalan (fruit and tree of Terminalia chebula)
parole.testo: From Middle Persian [script needed] (hlylk' /⁠halīlag⁠/, “myrobalan”), from Sanskrit हरीतकी (harītakī), ultimately from a Dravidian source; compare Telugu కరక (karaka).

parole.significato: tree and fruit of bastard myrobalan (Terminalia bellirica)
parole.testo: From Middle Persian [script needed] (balīlag), from Sanskrit बिभीतक (bibhītaka), विभितक (vibhitaka) of this meaning.

parole.significato: a kind of small skiff with a curved bow, sambuq
parole.testo: From Middle Persian *sanbūk whence Classical Persian سنبک (sumbuk), from Sanskrit शम्बूक (śambūka, literally “snail-shell”), or less likely Malay sampan, from Chinese 舢板 (MC paenX). parole.significato: cress (Lepidium spp., especially dittander Lepidium latifolium)
parole.testo: From Middle Persian. Cognate to Classical Syriac ܨܝܛܪܓ, ܨܝܛܪܩ, Classical Persian شیتره (šaytara, šītara), شیترک (šaytarak, šītarak). Do not confuse with شَاهْتَرَج (šāhtaraj, “fumitory”). If not ultimately identical to it, possibly from Sanskrit चित्रक (citraka, “doctorbush (Plumbago zeylanica)”).
